title: Traffic cadence & sentinel DSL for safe model rollouts
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Implement a declarative DSL and runtime 'Sentinel' that encodes traffic cadence (step schedules, hold windows, ramp curves), split strategies (weighted, header-based AB, shadow mirroring), and guardrail policies (SLO thresholds, error budget checks, regression detectors) to enable safe canary/A-B/blue-green rollouts with automatic and explainable rollback. Scope: API surface, controller that compiles DSL into routing rules, integration tests, Console UI hooks (preview + timeline), and alerting/playbook links. Does NOT cover dedicated capacity autoscaler tuning which is a follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: DSL syntax supports: steps, hold_ms, ramp_pct, split_key and mirror directives
Controller compiles DSL to routing config persisted in runtime config-store and applied to router within 10s of change under normal load
Guardrails evaluate: response_latency_p95, generation_error_rate, token-inflation-delta with configurable window and trigger severity
Auto-rollback triggers a canary revert + notification + audit entry, with manual override possible from Console
Integration tests simulate traffic and assert rollback occurs when synthetic workload violates thresholds
Console shows timeline preview and per-step metrics; audit log includes DSL diff and who applied it
implementation_notes: We will express cadence as a list of ordered steps; each step accepts duration (ms), target_percent, allow_shadow boolean and a list of guard expressions.
Guard expressions are evaluated against the metrics plane (Prometheus-derived time series) via the existing eval-worker; add new eval adaptor to compute token-inflation-delta metric.
Controller runs in leader-elected mode and writes compiled route to config-store (etcd). Runtime router watches config-store and applies atomically.
Auto-rollback will trigger a reversible config change that pins traffic back to previous stable variant and emits a traceable event id.
To reduce noise, require 2 consecutive evaluation windows (configurable) before auto-rollback; the default window is 60s and consecutive_count is 2.
Shadow (mirror) traffic will be sampled at a stable rate and annotated for billing but not counted towards SLO by default unless explicitly enabled in DSL.
We will provide a CLI preview tool that simulates step durations and expected cumulative exposure for compliance teams.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: Use a compact YAML-first DSL rather than a heavy policy engine to keep config reviewable by product teams. Rationale: faster iteration and easier auditability.
Tradeoff: Shorter evaluation windows reduce detection latency but increase false positives from noisy metrics; chosen default balances detection (60s x2) vs false positives.
Decision: Mirror traffic not counted in SLO by default to avoid spurious rollbacks from offloaded workloads; ops can opt-in per-rollout.
Tradeoff: Atomic application of routing config requires router restart path for certain kernel switches; we prefer soft-swap where possible to avoid p99 spikes.
Decision: Integrate with existing eval-worker instead of shipping a new metrics pipeline to accelerate delivery, accepting some complexity in adaptor code.
risks: Risk: Race between controller update and router application could cause transient duplicate exposure; mitigation: add sequence-numbered config versions and leader short-circuit guard.
Risk: Metric cardinality explosion if users define many split_keys; mitigation: limit derived series and aggregate on router for high-cardinality keys.
Risk: Autoscaling interplay — aggressive rollouts may create burst load; mitigation: add optional pre-rollout resource check step in DSL.
testing_plan: Unit tests for DSL parser & schema validation
End-to-end tests: synthetic traffic generator validates ramp curves and mock metric violations trigger rollback
Chaos test: randomly delay controller->router apply to validate graceful handling
Integration test with Console: render timeline and simulate manual override via UI workflow
qa_checklist: Security review of DSL injection vectors - ensure only authorized principals can create rollouts
Audit log entries recorded for all automatic rollbacks
Performance benchmark: controller latency from apply to router-ready < 10s in QA cluster
Verify no additional cost leakage for shadow traffic unless opt-in

notes_for_oncall: If auto-rollback triggers unexpectedly, oncall should: 1) confirm metric anomalies in dashboards, 2) check controller leader logs for errors, 3) if safe, perform manual override from Console and open incident ticket referencing this task.
